title: Geometry and separable field change of reduced algebraic normalization
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $X$ a reduced scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme] of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Define $X^
u$ as the disjoint union of the normalizations [def-sc-normalization] of the finitely many irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $X$, with their reduced induced structures, and let $
u:X^
u	o X$ be the canonical map. Then $
u$ is finite and surjective [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. The subset $N\subseteq X$ of points whose local rings are integrally closed domains [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] is a dense open, and $
u^{-1}(N)	o N$ is an isomorphism. For every open subscheme $W\subseteq X$, $
u^{-1}(W)	o W$ is canonically the normalization of $W$. If $K/k$ is a separable field extension [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension] (every finitely generated subextension is separably generated), the canonical comparison $(X_K)^
u	o X^
u	imes_k K$ is an isomorphism over $X_K=X	imes_k K$ [def-pc-base-change]; no algebraicity or finiteness of $K/k$ is assumed. In particular this comparison is an isomorphism for every extension of an algebraically closed base field $k$.

source.place: Tags 0BXR (lemma-normalization-locally-algebraic), 0C3N (lemma-normalization-and-change-of-fields); Morphisms Tags 035Q (lemma-normalization-normal), 035K (lemma-normalization-localization), 0CDV (lemma-normalization-in-terms-of-components). The normal locus equals the isomorphism locus: on an affine chart Spec A with finite integral closure B, it is the complement of the support of the finite A-module B/A.

proof.text: Finite type over a field and quasi-compactness make X Noetherian, so its irreducible components are finite in number. Their reduced induced schemes are integral: the vanishing ideal gives reducedness and the underlying component is irreducible. Normalize each component. The resulting maps to X are finite; their finite coproduct is finite (IsFinite.sigmaDesc). Every point belongs to a component and lifts through its surjective normalization. The coproduct normalization has normal stalks: each coproduct chart is the normalization of an integral component and normality transports through its open-immersion stalk isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 0CDV, 035Q; Varieties Tag 0BXR. Finite coproduct and stalk computations are written explicitly in Lean.

proof.text: Let x have an integrally closed domain stalk. Mathlib Scheme.exists_germ_injective gives an affine neighborhood V whose section ring injects into that stalk, hence V is integral. Exactly one ambient irreducible component C meets V: pulling any such component back to V gives its unique component; density of the intersection in the ambient component identifies that component with the closure of V. The reduced component inclusion restricted over V is a surjective closed immersion into the reduced scheme V, hence is an isomorphism. Thus Spec O_X,x maps dominantly to C. Its stalks are integrally closed, by localization and Spec.stalkIso. Apply the dominant normalization lifting theorem to get a dominant map a:Spec O_X,x -> C^nu. Compose with the coproduct inclusion. Mathlib spread_out_of_isGermInjective' (Tag 0BX6), applied to the finite normalization, spreads this into a section over a neighborhood W of x. Replace W by U=W intersect V. Only C^nu meets the inverse image of U, so that inverse image embeds openly into C^nu. The section is dominant there because a is dominant and factors through it. It is a closed immersion because it is a section of a separated morphism. Its closed dense image is the entire inverse image, and a surjective closed immersion into a reduced scheme is an isomorphism. Consequently normalization is an isomorphism over U.

proof.text: Take N to be the maximal open on which normalization is an isomorphism. It is an isomorphism over N by target-locality of isomorphisms. A point of N has normal stalk because the normalization has normal stalks and an open immersion induces stalk isomorphisms. Conversely the preceding local construction places every normal point in N. Generic stalks of a reduced Noetherian scheme are fields (Mathlib isField_stalk_of_closure_mem_irreducibleComponents); N therefore contains every generic point and is dense.

source.place: Tag 035Q and the generic-stalk field criterion; maximal open construction in WeilConjectures.Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.IsIso.

proof.text: For any dense open U of X, its inverse image in the normalization is dense. Indeed every irreducible component meets U: remove the other finitely many components, obtaining an open dense in that component, and intersect with U. Surjectivity of the component normalization makes the inverse image nonempty, hence dense in that integral normalization; continuity and the coproduct open cover give density in the whole normalization. Compare this normalization with any finite normal X-scheme which is isomorphic to X over a dense open having dense inverse image. Intersect that open with N and apply the finite-normal dense-open isomorphism theorem. Uniqueness follows from equality on the dense open, reducedness of the source and separatedness of the target.

source.place: Tag 0BQL, uniqueness of finite normal extensions from a dense open; elementary component topology.

proof.text: For an arbitrary open W of X, both its componentwise normalization and the restriction of X^nu are finite and normal over W. They are isomorphic to W over the intersection with N. Open immersions pull dense subsets back to dense subsets; the preceding inverse-image argument verifies density in both finite sources. Apply the comparison just established. Its over-W equation and separated-target uniqueness are precisely the required existence and uniqueness statement. Since X is Noetherian, the open W remains quasi-compact over k.

source.place: Tag 035K, normalization and open restriction; finite normal comparison provides the alternative to explicit localization and gluing.

proof.text: For a separable extension K/k, use affine charts and the tensor-product description of pullbacks of affine spectra. The normal-algebra scalar-extension theorem proves normality of the stalks of X^nu times_k K, transported through the affine pullback isomorphisms and cover stalk maps. The projection Spec K -> Spec k is flat because modules over a field are flat. The base-changed normalization is schematically dominant by flat base change, so its reduced source implies reducedness of X_K. It is finite. The inverse image of N is dense in X_K and its inverse image is dense in X^nu times_k K, since the projections along field extension are open and the original inverse image of N is dense. It is an isomorphism over this open, by pullback pasting. Apply finite normal comparison with the componentwise normalization of X_K. Pullback extensionality identifies the over-X_K equation with the two stated projection equations; thus uniqueness is exactly the requested uniqueness.

source.place: Varieties Tags 0C3N and 0C3M. Flat schematic dominance, openness and affine pullback identifications are Mathlib APIs.

proof.text: An algebraically closed field is perfect. Every finitely generated intermediate field of K/k is an essentially finite type field extension, so the separating transcendence-basis theorem makes it separably generated. This is exactly Algebra.IsSeparableExtension k K. Apply the preceding comparison, without imposing algebraicity or finiteness on K/k.
